title: The T.O.B.A. circuit: four or five shows a day
summary: She says T.O.B.A. time in Texas and Louisiana was slavery for the number of shows, though rooming houses and treatment were fine, and trains were segregated.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did you ever travel in the -- did you ever do the T.O.B.A. circuit?
Yeah, Lord, Lord. (Inaudible). I know
all about that mess. Well, would you tell me a little bit about it?

Yeah, T.O.B.A. circuit (unintelligible) always had to do four and five shows a day, slaves. And when I got off of that T.O.B. time, I got over on this other time, (inaudible). But T.O.B. time was nothing but slavery.
Why do you -- why was it slavery? Because they didn't pay you enough money?
(Unintelligible) tell you you had to do four and five shows a day, everyday. Four and five shows a day.
Where did you do those four and five shows a day?
All through Texas, all through Louisiana, all through New Orleans (unintelligible) quit in New Orleans. But Texas, Louisiana.
Uh-huh. And do you remember when you did those, when you traveled on that circuit? Do you remember what year that was?
Lord, no.
That was in the '20s, wasn't it?
(Unintelligible).
Uh-huh. That was in the '20s.
Oh, yeah, uh-huh.
And how did you travel on that circuit? Did you go on the train?
Yeah, on the train.
Train?
Uh-huh. We would always go on the train.
But you had to ride in the car for coloreds, didn't you?
(Unintelligible) train.
Yeah. But didn't you have to ride in the colored car on the train?
(Unintelligible) for colored. You had to (inaudible).
How did you feel about that?
Made me feel (unintelligible). So it didn't bother me.
Uh-huh. And when you were on that T.O.B.A. circuit, where did you sleep at night?
(Unintelligible) overnight ride.
You would have an overnight ride?
Just an overnight ride, that's all.
Uh-huh. So did you sleep on the train?
Never did.
You never slept on the train.
(Unintelligible).
Well, where did you -- what kind of place did you sleep in when you were on that circuit?
Just overnight -- usually took place around 11:30, 12:00 o'clock. You'd have your room (unintelligible) station to take -- I can take three and I can take two.
We're going to quiet them down now. Now, okay, they could take two and they could take three. Where did they take you, to somebody's house?
To a room. A man owned a house, a hotel or something.
I see. A rooming house, a hotel?
Uh-huh.
Uh-huh. And you all had the man who booked the show in would always look out of the way for a place -- places for people to stay.
Uh-huh. Was that all right?
Well, yeah. Same way it was in London.
Uh-huh.
(Unintelligible) in London (unintelligible) and they'd tell you just sign your name, your room is 2-7, 3-7, and so like -- you know.
So that was not like going to hotels today. That was very different, wasn't it?
Uh-huh.
And did you get your meals there too, in
Sometimes you'd get room and board.
Uh-huh.
Most of them would be room and board. (Unintelligible) wouldn't know where the room and board (unintelligible).
Uh-huh. Well, how were you treated? How was the room and board?
Very nice.
It was nice on the T.O.B.A.?
Uh-huh.
But you said it wasn't nice. You said it was like slavery.
Yeah, at the ______.
What?
Had to do so many shows.
Oh, I see. The work was hard, but the treatment was all right.
Uh-huh.
Is that it?
Uh-huh.
I see.
Had to do four or five shows a day.
